# Sonnet vs best DB vs ≥k-DB ensembles — overall accuracy on 147-gene bench

> **Supplementary Figure 5.** Ensembling the five gold-standard surface databases does not close the accuracy gap to the Sonnet 4.6 triage agent. Overall accuracy on the 147 protein-coding gene SurfaceBench (soft-credit rule: a contextually-surface protein counts correct when called surface) is shown for six predictors: the production triage agent (Sonnet 4.6 with gene identifiers; mean of three replicates), the single best-performing database, and four ensemble predictors requiring at least two, three, four, or all five databases to agree. Each database (UniProt, GO cellular component, HPA, SURFY, CSPA) is applied under the surface threshold that maximizes its own accuracy, so every predictor competes at its best. Requiring more databases to agree degrades accuracy monotonically: combining the databases suppresses surface calls faster than it corrects them and never recovers the proteins they jointly miss.
<!-- END manuscript-legend -->

Seven-bar comparison of overall verdict accuracy on the 147-gene
triage benchmark:

* **Sonnet (+ IDs)** — Claude Sonnet 4.6 triage agent on its
  canonical NCBI-resolver ("gene identifiers") prompt variant. The bar
  is the mean of the three per-replicate accuracies, with an SEM error
  bar and the individual replicates shown as dots.
* **UniProt (TM+signal)** — best single classical DB under its
  bench-optimized cutoff (TM OR signal-peptide positive)
* **1+ / 2+ / 3+ / 4+ / 5+ DB** — ensemble callers: "yes" iff at least
  k of the 5 surface DBs (UniProt, GO CC, HPA, SURFY, CSPA, each
  under its own optimized cutoff) vote yes. k=1 is the union (any DB);
  k=5 is the strict intersection of all 5.

Accuracy uses the project's soft-credit rule: yes ≡ contextual on
the positive side; `no` matches `no` only. Per-bucket breakdown
(yes / contextual / no) lives in the sibling `db_correctness_by_class`
figure.

Run:

```
uv run make_ensemble_vs_best_db_vs_sonnet.py
```

Data: the script reads only the bundled
`ensemble_vs_best_db_vs_sonnet.tsv` — one row per gene × model ×
prompt variant × replicate on the bench, with the truth labels, the 5
per-DB surface flags and the optimized UniProt / CSPA cutoffs
denormalized in. Built by `scripts/build_figure_tsvs.py`.
